1mh01mp:93: Evals verify implementation quality (whether outputs meet standards), while experiments validate business impact (whether users truly benefit). The more complex the system, the more you need to bound the risk; you cannot rely solely on evals when making launch decisions.
1ngtfqk:171: However, evals also have blind spots. The Spotify team revealed that about 42% of their shipped experiments needed rollback due to secondary metric regressions: decreased session length, increased crash rate, retention erosion. None of these issues were flagged in advance by any evals or offline evaluations. This shows that evals measure one dimension of implementation quality, while experiments quantify real end-user impact in the production system. The dimensions not measured may be exactly the ones that determine success or failure.
